How QoS is enforced

Method, as implemented in qos_policy.py and the controller

DiffServ classes follow RFC 4594 service-class guidance: EF (46) for voice, AF41 (34) for multimedia conferencing, AF21 (18) for low-latency data, CS1 (8) for low-priority data, and 0 for best effort. The policy is data — class names, DSCP values, capacity shares, queue and meter ids — and loading it validates that no DSCP is claimed twice, every share lies in (0, 1], and the shares cannot overcommit the link.

Meter rates are never stored as absolute numbers. meter_bands() derives each rate from the link capacity supplied at install time (share × capacity, with a burst allowance of 100 ms of the rate), so the same policy is correct on a 10 Mbps teaching link and a 10 Gbps one. The capacities tabulated on this page are the ones the recordings themselves declare, plus the controller's own default.

In the controller, meters are installed on every switch when it connects, and each access-switch packet-in is classified by its DSCP (the IPv4 TOS byte shifted by two) through class_for_dscp(); the flow is then installed with that class's meter attached. Unmarked traffic falls into the default class and is unmetered. Live runs enable this with SDN_QOS=1, set by the live guest for every run.
